prompt: Which functional groups in a target molecule suggest that it might come from an aldol reaction?

choices.text: A β-hydroxy aldehyde or ketone, or a conjugated enone
A γ-hydroxy ketone or a nonconjugated enone
choices.why: An aldol product has its –OH on the β carbon, and dehydration gives a C=C conjugated with the carbonyl group.

choices.text: An ester or a carboxylic acid
choices.why: The aldol reaction joins aldehydes or ketones and gives β-hydroxy carbonyl compounds or enones.
Neither group is formed by an aldol reaction.

explanation: The aldol reaction gives either a β-hydroxy aldehyde/ketone or an α,β-unsaturated aldehyde/ketone, depending on conditions. Whenever a target contains either group, it might come from an aldol reaction.

prompt: Which of these compounds could be an aldol condensation product (Exercise 23.4.1)?

choices.why: Its –OH is on carbon 2, the α carbon. Aldol products have the –OH on the β carbon.
Its –OH is three carbons from the carbonyl carbon (a γ-hydroxy ketone), not on the β carbon.
Its C=C is not conjugated with the carbonyl group, so it isn't an aldol enone.

explanation: 5-Ethyl-4-methyl-4-hepten-3-one, CH3CH2COC(CH3)=C(CH2CH3)2, is a conjugated enone, with the C=C between the α and β carbons. It is the aldol condensation product of 3-pentanone.

prompt: Which compound gives 5-ethyl-4-methyl-4-hepten-3-one in an aldol condensation?

choices.why: Butanal is an aldehyde and gives an eight-carbon product, 2-ethyl-2-hexenal; the target is a ten-carbon ketone.
Two propanal molecules give only a six-carbon product, and it is an aldehyde.
Two 3-hexanone molecules would give a twelve-carbon product; the target has ten carbons.

explanation: The target, CH3CH2COC(CH3)=C(CH2CH3)2, is C10H18O. Working backward, the α carbon of one 3-pentanone (bearing a methyl group) bonded to the carbonyl carbon of a second 3-pentanone (bearing two ethyl groups), and water was lost: 2 C5H10O − H2O = C10H18O.

prompt: From which compound is 2-ethyl-1-hexanol, an alcohol used to make plasticizers, prepared commercially by an aldol route?

choices.why: Two acetaldehyde molecules give a four-carbon product; 2-ethyl-1-hexanol has eight carbons.
Two hexanal molecules would give a twelve-carbon product.
2-Ethylhexanal is an intermediate in the route, formed after the aldol step; it is not the starting material.

explanation: Working backward: 2-ethyl-1-hexanol comes from 2-ethylhexanal by reduction; 2-ethylhexanal from catalytic reduction of 2-ethyl-2-hexenal; and 2-ethyl-2-hexenal is the aldol condensation product of butanal.

prompt: In the industrial synthesis of 2-ethyl-1-hexanol, which compound is the aldol condensation product of butanal?

choices.why: 2-Ethylhexanal has no C=C. It is made from the aldol product by catalytic hydrogenation.
That is the final product, made by reducing the aldehyde group of 2-ethylhexanal.
Octanal is unbranched. The aldol product of butanal branches at carbon 2, where the ethyl group is.

explanation: Butanal with KOH in ethanol gives 2-ethyl-2-hexenal, the aldol condensation product. H2 over platinum then gives 2-ethylhexanal, and a final reduction gives 2-ethyl-1-hexanol.

prompt: Which step converts 2-ethyl-2-hexenal into 2-ethylhexanal in the industrial route to 2-ethyl-1-hexanol?

choices.text: Catalytic hydrogenation with H2 over platinum

choices.why: KOH in ethanol carries out the aldol condensation of butanal, the step before.
That is the final step, which turns 2-ethylhexanal into 2-ethyl-1-hexanol. Here the C=C must be reduced.

choices.text: Heating with acid to remove water
choices.why: Water was already lost when the enone formed; 2-ethyl-2-hexenal has no –OH to remove.

explanation: 2-Ethyl-2-hexenal is reduced by catalytic hydrogenation (H2/Pt), which saturates the C=C bond and gives 2-ethylhexanal. In the same way, a saturated ketone can be made by hydrogenating an aldol enone.

prompt: How many molecules of butanal are combined to make one molecule of 2-ethyl-1-hexanol?
explanation: Butanal has four carbons and 2-ethyl-1-hexanol has eight. The aldol reaction joins two butanal molecules to give 2-ethyl-2-hexenal, which is then reduced twice to the alcohol.

prompt: Butanal is C4H8O. How many hydrogen atoms does 2-ethyl-2-hexenal, its aldol condensation product, contain?
explanation: Two butanal molecules (C8H16O2) lose one H2O, giving C8H14O. 2-Ethyl-2-hexenal, CH3CH2CH2CH=C(CH2CH3)CHO, has 16 − 2 = 14 hydrogens.

prompt: 1-Butanol is prepared commercially by a route that begins with an aldol reaction, followed by LiAlH4 and then H2/Pd (Exercise 23.4.2). Which aldehyde does the route start from?

choices.why: Two propanal molecules give a six-carbon product, but 1-butanol has four carbons.
Two butanal molecules give an eight-carbon product; that is the route to 2-ethyl-1-hexanol.
Formaldehyde has no α hydrogen, so it can't form an enolate and undergo an aldol reaction with itself.

explanation: Two acetaldehyde molecules give 2-butenal in base (NaOH). LiAlH4 reduces the aldehyde to an alcohol, and H2/Pd reduces the C=C, giving the four-carbon alcohol 1-butanol.

prompt: Why can't 2-hydroxy-2-methylpentanal be an aldol product (Exercise 23.4.1)?

choices.text: Its –OH is on the α carbon rather than the β carbon
It is an aldehyde, and aldol products must be ketones
choices.why: Aldehydes give aldol products too; 3-hydroxybutanal, the original aldol, is an aldehyde.

choices.text: It has a methyl branch on carbon 2, next to the –CHO group
choices.why: Branching at carbon 2 is common; propanal gives 3-hydroxy-2-methylpentanal.

choices.text: It is a tertiary alcohol, which no aldol reaction can produce
choices.why: Aldol products can be tertiary alcohols; 4-hydroxy-4-methyl-2-pentanone is the aldol product of acetone.

explanation: In an aldol product the two oxygens have a 1,3 relationship: the –OH is on the β carbon. In 2-hydroxy-2-methylpentanal the –OH is on carbon 2, next to the –CHO carbon, so it is not an aldol product.
